newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA GETS GRANTS WORTH 475 MLN RAND FROM EU.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA GETS GRANTS WORTH 475 MLN RAND FROM EU.

text.p: Deputy Finance Minister Gill Marcus and European Union ambassador Erwan Fouere on Wednesday signed seven financing agreements worth 95 million ECU or 475 million rand.

The agreements covered some of the projects which will be funded from the EU's 1996 allocation of 130 million ECU or 650 million rand allocation for development projects in South Africa through the European Programme for Reconstruction and Development(EPRD).
EPRD funds are always allocated one year after initial negotiations about aid programmes and these allocations will be spent in 1997.

The balance of the 650 million rand will be used to fund non governmental organisations (NGOs). Fouere said this highlighted the fact that the EU had not, as some had claimed, abandoned NGOs at the expense of government programmes since the 1994 elctions.
Marcus said the grants were focused on specific sectors and included funding for a research project to raise competitiveness in the Southern African Development Community as a whole.

"It is very focused assistance...and these kinds of areas are very much to the forefront of the needs of the country," she said. "It is assistance in real terms...it helps. We are very grateful not only for the financial support but also for the technical support that goes with it."
Wedensday's signing was to be followed up by a meeting in April at which both sides would start discussing a three year programme involving 500 million ECU or 2.5 billion rand in aid from the EU.
"We will try to narrow the focus even more and we are looking for sectoral support programmes, particularly in education and health," Marcus said.
Support would also be sought for education and training and greater support for NGOs.

The seven agreements provide nine million ECU or 45 million rand for improving policing in the Eastern Cape, 15 million ECU or 75 million rand for the electrification of 1,000 rural schools in the Eastern Cape and Northern Province and 19.2 million CU or 96 million rand for a public service management development programme.

They also provide 17.2 million ECU or 86 million rand for technical support for the education department, 24.5 million ECU or 122.5 million rand for the Cato Manor Development Programme, 8.9 million ECU or 44 million rand for small business developmet and 1.1 million ECU or 5.5 million rand for a SADC finance and investment sector research project.

Fouere said the agreements once again underscored the EU's commitment to helping a democratic South Africa meet its development goals. The grant for a SADC programme highlighted the catalytic role that South Africa was playing in the development of th region.
